cap_note: 2019/20 restart: every remaining match behind closed doors, at most 300 key people in each stadium. The last match with a crowd before the suspension was on 2020-03-09.
2020/21 began behind closed doors. No Premier League pilot match with spectators was found (the Championship had two on 2020-09-19).

England tiers from 2020-12-02: tier 1 up to 4,000 or 50% of capacity, tier 2 up to 2,000 or 50% (whichever lower), tier 3 none. Depends on the club: clubs in tier 3 areas stayed closed; no away fans. London moved to tier 3 on 2020-12-16. Tier 2 was removed on 2020-12-30 (en.wikipedia Championship article), so the end date is approximate; the only E0 match on 2020-12-30 (Newcastle v Liverpool) was in a tier 3 area.
Behind closed doors again: no tier 2 areas remained, and a third national lockdown was announced on 2021-01-04.

Step 3 from 2021-05-17: largest outdoor seated venues up to 10,000 or a quarter of capacity, whichever lower (gov.uk; en.wikipedia wrongly says 'whichever was higher'). Home fans only. Rounds played on 18-19 and 23 May.
2019/20 restart (regular season), behind closed doors.
2020/21 began behind closed doors.
EFL pilots: Norwich v Preston and Middlesbrough v Bournemouth with 1,000 spectators. Every other match that day was behind closed doors.
Pilots put on hold after cases rose from late September; second national lockdown in November.

Tier 2 clubs up to 2,000 (Luton and Wycombe capped at 1,000: no earlier pilot); tier 3 clubs none. Brentford, Millwall, QPR and Watford closed again from 2020-12-16. Luton, Reading and Wycombe closed from 2020-12-19, when Bristol City opened. From 2020-12-23 only Bournemouth were eligible. Tier 2 was removed on 2020-12-30. Welsh clubs (Cardiff, Swansea) follow Welsh rules, not checked.
Closed for the rest of the regular season. The play-offs (May 2021, up to 20% of capacity) are not league matches.
Only Eibar v Real Sociedad (rearranged round 24), played behind closed doors after LaLiga's 10 March decision. The league was suspended on 2020-03-12.
2019/20 restart behind closed doors (es.wikipedia attendance is 0 for every match from round 28).
es.wikipedia per-match attendance is 0 for every match in rounds 1-36.

Only in regions in phase 1 (Valencia, Galicia, Balearic Islands, Murcia on 2021-05-14): up to 30% of capacity, at most 5,000. es.wikipedia attendance: Valencia v Eibar 3,000 and Villarreal v Sevilla 5,000 (16 May); Levante v Cadiz 5,000 (21 May); Celta v Betis 2,686 and Elche v Athletic 5,000 (22 May). All other matches 0.
2019/20 restart behind closed doors (es.wikipedia attendance 0 from round 32). Fuenlabrada v Deportivo, postponed from 20 July after Fuenlabrada positives, was played on 7 August.
es.wikipedia per-match attendance is 0 for every match in rounds 1-38.

Same rule as SP1 (phase-1 regions, up to 30% of capacity, at most 5,000). es.wikipedia attendance: Castellon v Ponferradina 2,640 and Lugo v Mirandes 1,700 (15 May); Mallorca v Alcorcon 4,086 (16 May); Cartagena v Almeria 2,240 (18 May); Castellon v Rayo 4,650 and Lugo v Cartagena 2,134 (24 May); Cartagena v Girona 4,531 and Sporting v Almeria 4,500 (30 May). All other matches 0.

Government decree of 4 March 2020 closed all stadiums until 3 April (FIGC C.U. 173: Serie A behind closed doors). Postponed round-26 matches played 8-9 March, then the league was suspended. In the round of 29 Feb-1 Mar the matches in affected regions were postponed rather than played behind closed doors.
2019/20 restart behind closed doors.

Up to 1,000 spectators: government-regions agreement of 19 Sep 2020 for every Serie A match from 20 Sep, and the decree in force from 13 Oct set 1,000 outdoors. The two 19 Sep matches came before the agreement (Verona v Roma was invitation only; Fiorentina v Torino not checked).

Decree signed 24 Oct, in force 26 Oct: sport only 'senza la presenza di pubblico'. The general reopening of national sporting events to the public came only from 1 June 2021 (yellow zones), after the season; no Serie A match with spectators in this period was found.

PARTIAL: rounds 26-27 played behind closed doors only at stadiums in northern Italy (decree of 25 Feb 2020 for Emilia-Romagna, Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Lombardy, Veneto, Piedmont, Liguria). Elsewhere crowds were normal. Affected matches not listed one by one.

Decree of 4 March 2020: all stadiums closed until 3 April; round 28 played 7-9 March, then suspended. Start boundary inferred from the decree (it.wikipedia's Serie B text names only rounds 26-27; en.wikipedia says 'starting 8 March').
2019/20 restart (Cremonese v Ascoli rearranged on 17 June), behind closed doors. Regular season ended 31 July.

UNCERTAIN, at most 1,000. The national allowance of 19 Sep 2020 covered Serie A only. The decree in force from 13 Oct set 1,000 outdoors for national events. Regional orders (Veneto, Emilia-Romagna, Lombardy) may have admitted fans earlier. Which Serie B matches had spectators is not verified.
Decree in force 26 Oct 2020: no public. Regular season ended 10 May 2021, before the general reopening of 1 June 2021.
Gladbach v Koln (rearranged), the first ghost game in Bundesliga history. Round 26 (13-16 March) was to be behind closed doors but was postponed.
2019/20 restart (matchdays 26-34), ghost games throughout.

Agreement of 15 Sep 2020: up to 20% of stadium capacity, decided by each local health authority. 22 of the 54 matches on matchdays 1-6 were behind closed doors (Bayern v Schalke on 18 Sep among them); about 2,900 were admitted on average. Leipzig allowed 8,500 and Berlin up to 5,000. Matchday 6 (30 Oct-2 Nov) is uncertain: de.wikipedia's season text dates the general exclusion from matchday 7, but its stadium table says from matchday 6.
Federal-state decision of 28 Oct 2020: no spectators in November (measures from 2 Nov). The exclusion lasted until the final matchday.
Final matchday: a small number of spectators allowed at selected matches; the most was 2,000 at Union Berlin v RB Leipzig. The other matches were behind closed doors.
2019/20 restart (matchdays 26-34), ghost games throughout. en.wikipedia counts only the matches after 9 March 2020 as behind closed doors.
Same 20% concept as D1. 13 of the 54 matches on matchdays 1-6 were behind closed doors; just over 1,900 were admitted on average.
Ghost games from matchday 7 (decision of 28 Oct 2020). The only exception: 250 spectators at Hamburg v Braunschweig on the final matchday (2021-05-23).

National cap of 5,000 per event (announced 11 Aug 2020, to 30 Oct 2020). Local orders cut crowds further in some areas; these were not checked one by one. fr.wikipedia round totals fall from 42,391 (round 2) to 14,280 (round 8).
From 30 Oct 2020 gatherings of more than 30 people were banned and every match was behind closed doors. fr.wikipedia per-round attendance is 0 for rounds 9-38.

Lens v Orleans (round 28, Monday 9 March) behind closed doors under the ban on gatherings over 1,000 from 9 March. The rest of round 28 (6-7 March) had crowds, and the season was then suspended. fr.wikipedia dates 'the' first closed-doors Ligue 2 match to 8 March without naming it.
National cap of 5,000 per event until 30 Oct 2020; local orders lower in some areas (lowest crowd 339, Toulouse v Troyes on 3 Oct).
Behind closed doors from 30 Oct 2020 (gatherings of more than 30 banned); fr.wikipedia per-round attendance is 0 for rounds 9-38.
